input: nums has at most 100 integers in [1,100]; empty input is accepted. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Exact sum, without a modulus, of squared distinct-value counts over all nonempty contiguous subarrays.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Each square is at most 10000 and at most 5050 subarrays exist, so the total is at most 50500000 and exact. This is problem 2913, not the larger modular variant. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n^2+1) time and O(n+1) live auxiliary set space; each start builds a fresh set and every extended subarray is counted. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 355 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used.
